findings.summary: Track names (index-tracking, S&P 500, flexible, money-market) mean nothing to the reader, and nothing shows which track is safe like a deposit, so they can't pick a track.
The bond tracks the reader would trust show no return, only 'less than 3 years', so the reader can't judge them.
Dark page with small grey headers and dotted underlines is hard to read even when enlarged.
Too many numbers per row and very long lines; the reader lost their place in the table.
Returns are shown before management fees, so the reader doesn't know the real return. Fees appear in their own column.
Nothing compares returns or fees to a bank deposit. This is a wish for more.
Big returns (24%, 26%) catch the eye and make the page feel like it's for gamblers. This is an emotional reaction, not something that blocks use.
The reader couldn't tell what the yellow and turquoise ring charts in the exposure column mean. This is a different issue from rings in two shades of teal.
Unexplained marks on screens 4-5: '!' with 'not yet reported', '101%', and arrow icons.
